articles.headline: Meta's New Ads Ranking System Uses User Sequence Data Instead of Static Features
articles.body: Meta has unveiled a multi-stage architecture for ads ranking that fundamentally shifts how the platform predicts which ads users will engage with. Instead of relying on manually engineered sparse features, the new system models the order and timing of user actions—what researchers call sequence learning—to capture individual preferences and intent across products, ads, and content. This approach processes billions of daily user interactions across Meta's recommendation platforms, transforming raw temporal signals into predictive power. The key innovation is treating user behavior as a sequence of events rather than isolated data points, which means the system understands not just what a user did, but when they did it and in what order. This matters because the timing and context of actions reveal intent signals that static features miss entirely. The system uses scaling laws to improve performance as it processes more data, suggesting that accuracy will continue improving as Meta feeds it more user sequences. For advertisers, this translates to better audience targeting, higher relevance scores, and—critically—lower wasted ad spend on mismatched users. The architecture was built on Meta's 2024 research into sequence learning for recommendations, which demonstrated that temporal modeling outperforms traditional feature engineering approaches on recommendation benchmarks.

Detect intent shifts mid-session: user browsing furniture, then suddenly searching prices—serve high-intent ads immediately.

articles.headline: Meta Open-Sources Kernel Scheduler to Protect Ad Latency During Linux Upgrades
articles.body: Meta has turned to sched_ext, an upstream BPF-based extensible scheduling framework, to solve a critical infrastructure challenge: protecting ad-serving latency when upgrading Linux kernels across its massive fleet. At Meta's scale, even a few milliseconds of latency degradation can significantly harm ad performance and revenue. The company developed a custom scheduling policy specifically optimized for ads delivery using the open-source sched_ext framework, allowing them to upgrade kernel versions without risking the latency regressions that typically occur during such migrations. This approach represents a shift toward using BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) to extend kernel capabilities at runtime, rather than maintaining custom kernel forks or accepting performance trade-offs. By open-sourcing this work, Meta is contributing back to the upstream Linux ecosystem while solving a problem that likely affects other large-scale infrastructure operators running time-sensitive services.
examples: Upgrade Linux kernels without millisecond latency spikes tanking ad delivery performance.
Custom scheduling policies adapt to ads workloads in real-time via BPF.
Run complex scheduling logic in user-space, not baked into the kernel.
articles.build: Infrastructure firms managing high-frequency trading, payment processing, or ad-tech systems are adopting custom kernel scheduling to eliminate latency regressions—charging clients $50k–$500k annually for tailored performance optimization. This move signals Google's commitment to understanding how AI technologies impact economies, labor markets, and business models at scale. The expansion suggests Google is investing heavily in research that goes beyond pure AI capability development and into the real-world economic implications of AI deployment. By recruiting top academic talent, Google is positioning itself to shape policy conversations and maintain thought leadership as governments and institutions grapple with AI's economic impact. The team will likely focus on areas like workforce transformation, productivity gains, market dynamics, and how different industries are monetizing AI capabilities. This type of foundational research typically informs both Google's internal product strategy and its public positioning on AI regulation and economic policy.
examples: Academic researchers analyze how AI adoption affects labor market wages and job creation across industries.
Fellows study enterprise AI productivity gains and measure ROI for businesses implementing Google AI tools.
Internal teams model economic scenarios for AI-driven automation and forecast market transformation timelines.
articles.build: Consultants are charging $5,000–$25,000 per month to help enterprises understand AI's economic impact on their operations and workforce planning. Freelance researchers on platforms like Upwork are earning $50–$150/hour analyzing AI adoption trends for corporate clients preparing for board presentations. Training companies are selling $10,000+ workshops to HR and operations teams on preparing for AI-driven economic shifts.

articles.hook: Meta's been quietly building Python's future for a decade straight.
articles.headline: Meta Hits 10-Year Milestone as Python Software Foundation Sponsor
articles.body: Meta has reached a significant milestone in its commitment to open-source infrastructure: a full decade of consecutive sponsorship of the Python Software Foundation (PSF), the nonprofit organization responsible for advancing, supporting, and protecting Python and its global developer community. Python remains one of the world's most influential and widely-used programming languages, and Meta uses it extensively across its entire engineering stack — from backend systems to AI infrastructure to developer tooling. This long-term sponsorship underscores how critical Python has become to Meta's operations and its broader strategic bet on open-source ecosystems. By funding the PSF year after year, Meta ensures the language continues evolving while maintaining the collaborative, community-driven ethos that made Python indispensable to machine learning, data science, and enterprise development. The commitment also signals Meta's philosophy: strategic investments in foundational infrastructure generate compounding returns across the entire tech industry. For context, Python's dominance in AI and data science — areas where Meta is heavily investing — makes PSF support a high-ROI play that strengthens Meta's hiring pool, engineering culture, and industry influence simultaneously.
examples: Use Python to build AI models that run seamlessly across Meta's internal tools and production systems.
Access improved Python libraries and frameworks maintained by PSF-funded contributors worldwide.
Leverage Python's continuous evolution to keep your AI stack future-proof and compatible with enterprise standards.
articles.build: Freelance Python developers and AI engineers are charging $120–$250/hour to help companies migrate their data science pipelines to Python frameworks backed by Meta and other Fortune 500 sponsors. Mid-market consulting firms are landing $50K–$200K contracts to audit and optimize Python codebases for machine learning readiness. Open-source trainers are selling $2,000–$10,000 cohort-based courses on Python for AI, capitalizing on the language's status as the de facto standard.
